stick.name: Stick
stick.about: For crafting, and fuel for a campfire.

stone.name: Stone
stone.about: For tools and campfires. Try knocking two together.

twine.name: Twine
twine.about: Cut from tall grass. Ties tools together.

sharp-stone.name: Sharp stone
sharp-stone.about: Knocked off a stone. Cuts and shapes things, and you keep it when you do.

twig.name: Twig
twig.about: Cut from a stick. Kindling for a campfire, and it burns fast.

long-stick.name: Long stick
long-stick.about: Two sticks tied together. Long enough for a spear.

axe-head.name: Stone axe head
axe-head.about: A sharp stone wrapped in twine. Tie it to a long stick to make an axe.

pick-head.name: Stone pick head
pick-head.about: Two sharp stones tied back to back. Tie it to a long stick to make a pickaxe.

hoe-head.name: Stone hoe head
hoe-head.about: A flat stone wrapped in twine. Tie it to a long stick to make a hoe.

berry.name: Berry
berry.about: Picked from berry bushes. Eat one to feel less hungry.

berry-seeds.name: Berry seeds
berry-seeds.about: Cut from a berry. Plant them on a farm field and a berry bush grows in about a day.

fish.name: Raw fish
fish.about: Caught at the pond with a fishing spear. Cook it on a lit campfire before you eat it.

cooked-fish.name: Cooked fish
cooked-fish.about: Cooked on a campfire. Fills you up.

stone-hoe.name: Stone hoe
stone-hoe.about: Digs farm fields in your camp, and flattens them again. Tap the ground in your camp to dig one.

fishing-spear.name: Fishing spear
fishing-spear.about: For fishing. Tap the pond, then Fish.

log.name: Log
log.about: Chop it into sticks with an axe, or burn it on a campfire.

recipes.name: Stone knife
recipes.about: Cuts tall grass fast and picks 2 berries at a time
Cut a stick into 2 twigs with a sharp stone (you keep the stone)
Cut a berry open for its seeds with a sharp stone (you keep the stone)
Wrap a sharp stone in twine
Tie two sharp stones back to back with twine

recipes.name: Stone pickaxe
recipes.about: Breaks rocks and mines boulders for stones
Wrap a flat stone in twine

recipes.name: Stone hoe
recipes.about: Digs farm fields in your camp

recipes.name: Campfire
recipes.about: Place it, build it, then light it

recipes.name: Cooked fish
recipes.about: Raw fish can't be eaten. Cook it by a lit campfire (about 10 s)

help.settings: carryCapacity is the most weight a person can carry (tools on the tool bar don't count). toolSlots is how many spots the tool bar has (above the inventory): only tools on it get used, and they weigh nothing. walkSpeed is in metres per second. worldSize is how wide the square world is in metres (100 makes it 100 m x 100 m, with the clearing in the middle); it can be 40 to 300, and the bigger it is the more your phone has to draw. needsSpeed is 1 for real time; set it higher to test, for example 60 makes an hour of hunger and thirst pass in a minute. autoName fills in a name from testNames on the Make your person screen (handy while testing; set it to false for the real game). respawnMinutes is how often (online) the world adds one stick and one stone, if there are fewer on the ground than startInWorld: sticks under trees, stones by boulders. maxPlaying is how many people can play at once (20 for now, to stay inside Cloudflare's free plan); anyone else waits in line on the main menu and joins by themselves when a spot opens. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing it. worldTimeZone is the one clock the whole world runs on (date, time, day and night), the same for every player: Australia/Darwin for the Oceania world. craftSearchFrom: Craft shows a search box once you know this many recipes. fadeDays: things left lying on the ground fade away after this many days (0: never). Only what people put there (dropped, chopped, mined, a dead person's things, a campfire taken apart) and what the admin adds; the sticks and stones the world tops up by itself stay. Inside a camp the days don't run. The admin can change it live.
help.items: To add an item, copy one of the items above, give it a new id (lower case, no spaces) and set its name, plural, weight and look. It then shows up by itself in the Inventory, in Recipes (if a recipe makes it) and in the admin's Add list, with a picture drawn from its look. Shapes and their looks: rod (length, thickness, colour, twig, lashing: a twine colour tied round the middle, like a long stick), flake (size, colour: a sharp stone), head (head: axe or pick, colour, lashing: a stone tool head on its own, with twine round its middle), rock (size, colour), ball (size, colour, leaf: a colour or false), axe (length, thickness, colour, head, lashing), log (length, radius, colour, end), knife (length, thickness, colour, blade, lashing), coil (size, colour), campfire (size, colour, stone, ash), spear (length, thickness, colour, head, lashing), fish (length, colour, belly), box (width, height, depth, colour). An unknown shape is drawn as a rock. eat is what eating one gives (a berry gives hunger 10), which adds an Eat button in the inventory. tool: {"uses": 20} makes it a tool that wears out after that many uses (a wear bar in the inventory); a tool shows in your hand only while you use it (chopping, cutting), and only a tool on the tool bar (settings.toolSlots) gets used. startInWorld is how many lie around when the world starts (0 for things you can only make), and startNear is how many of those start close to where you appear. After changing items, run python3 tools/worlds.py test-build so the server knows about them. about (optional) is a short line shown when you tap it in the Inventory; without it, the about of the recipe that makes it is used. startInWorld: how many lie about the world; while there are fewer, one more turns up every settings.respawnMinutes, at a spot by spawnsNear (trees or boulders). A new item with startInWorld and spawnsNear starts turning up by itself, no reset needed (run tools/worlds.py test-build).
help.recipes: To add a recipe, put it in the recipes list like this: {"id": "stone-axe", "name": "Stone axe", "needs": {"axe-head": 1, "long-stick": 1, "twine": 1}, "makes": {"stone-axe": 1}, "about": "Chops trees"}. Every item in needs, keeps and makes must exist in items. Players make things on the craft mat (0.1.8), at the top of the inventory's Recipes tab (0.1.15): they tap a recipe in the list, the mat shows its things (what they don't have faded), and once they have its needs plus its keeps, Make lights up. Every craft mat recipe shows by itself in Recipes, greyed out while the player doesn't carry everything it takes (Luke, 0.1.12); tapping one puts its things on the mat, as many as it takes, and the mat shows that recipe until they change what's on it. The server keeps what each player has made (their next person keeps it too): the first make says Your first one! No mystery (Luke, 0.1.10): the mat always shows what the things on it make. Keep recipes simple: 2 or 3 things, at most 2 of each, and make big things from smaller steps (an axe head first, then the axe). No two recipes can want the same things on the mat (lint checks). keeps (optional) are tools the recipe needs on the mat but does not use up, like {"sharp-stone": 1} to cut a stick into a twig. about is a short line shown on the mat (optional). The server checks crafting too, so run python3 tools/worlds.py test-build after changing recipes. near (optional) is a placeable id, like campfire: the recipe can then only be made close to a built one (a fire has to be lit), and it is listed in that thing's tap menu under its craftLabel (Cook) without having to be made first. Use it for cooking. Food is only made at stations (Luke, 0.1.9): the craft mat never makes a recipe with near, it says where to make it instead (Cook this on a lit campfire), and Recipes only lists craft mat recipes. seconds (optional) is how long making it takes, like cooking at a fire (20): the things are used up when it finishes. group (optional) puts it under a button in Recipes (Tools, Food, Building, Clothes, Materials); without it tools go under Tools, food under Food, things you place under Building and the rest under Materials.
help.looks: Each list here is a set of choices on the Make your person screen. Add an entry to add a choice.
help.stats: Stats run in real time. Every stat goes from 0 to 100. perHour is how much it changes each real hour, and whileAsleep is used instead while sleeping. lowAt shows the warning (the ring pulses red, and under 10 it flashes). atZero is what happens to other stats each hour while this one is empty. Health heals (4 an hour, 8 asleep, so about a day to full) when nothing is empty, and the person dies when health reaches 0. fullLabel is shown when you try to eat or drink but don't need to. gainLabel is the word in the pop-up when eating or drinking fills it (+10 food, +15 water), since '+10 Hunger' would read like getting hungrier; without it the need's name is used. Hunger lasts about a day (a berry fills 10), thirst about 16 hours awake (a drink fills 15), Rest about 16 hours awake and 8 asleep (whileAsleepAtNight: faster at night, about 6 hours). With no water you die in about 3 days, with no food in about a week. collapseAtZero (Rest): when it runs out your person collapses asleep where they stand and can't be woken until it's back to wakeAt (25). Stamina (id energy) is not deadly. icon: heart, food, drop, moon or bolt. The server uses the same numbers (copied by tools/worlds.py).
help.sources: Things in the world you can use, matched by name ("Pond", "Berry bush"). action is the button in the tap menu, like "Drink". gives adds to stats each time (one drink at the pond gives 15 thirst). harvest is what one pick puts in your inventory (1 berry), holds is how many a full bush has (up to 15), and regrowHours is how long a picked-bare bush takes to grow them all back; picked berries grow back one at a time. seconds is how long it takes. pose is kneel, pick or bend. fish (the pond has it): action and verb are the tap menu button and the busy word, seconds how long a try takes, tool what you need to carry (it wears each try), catch what a catch gives, chance the share of tries that catch one (0.5), holds how many fish the pond has for everyone and regrowMinutes how often one comes back; the server keeps the count (run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing it). tool and toolHarvest: with that tool you get toolHarvest per pick instead (a knife picks 2 berries), and the tool wears.
help.defaultLook: How a new person starts on the Make your person screen.
help.daylight: Day and night follow the world's clock (settings.worldTimeZone), the same for every player; on the main menu a world that isn't open shows its own region's time. Each entry is how the world looks at that hour, and the game blends between them. sky is the haze colour, skyLight and groundLight light things from above and below, brightness is how strong that is, sun is the sun or moon colour, sunStrength how strong, sunHeight its angle in degrees.
help.version: version is the game version and build counts the test copies of that version (start build at 1 for each new version, count up for each test copy). Both only need changing here.
help.era: era only goes up if the version numbers are ever reset lower (they were once, 23 Nov 2026: 0.3.8 became 0.1.0), so games from before still get moved on to the newest version.
help.server: server is the address of the online world. The test link and the release both join the same live world (there's no separate test world). Leave it empty to play offline.
help.chatFilter: Words kept out of speech bubbles (shown as stars) and names (pick another). anywhere: caught even inside a longer word. words: only caught as a whole word (so 'class' is fine), plus endings like s, ed, ing. phrases: caught as a run of words. Numbers and symbols standing in for letters (sh1t, @ss) are caught too. The server gets a copy: tools/worlds.py test-build copies it to server/words.json. names: extra words only kept out of names, so nobody can pretend to be the admin.
help.away: How a person looks after themselves while their player is away (the server does this). near: 'pond' keeps them strolling round the main pond (anything else: round where you left them). wanderMin and wanderMax: how far in metres from there they stroll. strollSpeed in metres per second. While away they first carry on with what's left of their task list (the game sends it to the server, which does each task the same way: server/src/tasks.js), stopping to eat and drink as above and to sleep when tired (not just because it's night); things that have gone are skipped. Coming back, what's left of the list is back on your screen. They eat what they carry when hunger is under eatBelow, go for berries if they have none, and drink at the pond when thirst is under drinkBelow. After sleepAfterHours away they lie down asleep: hunger and thirst keep dropping slowly (the asleep rates) but stop at asleepFloor, so they can't die; after goneAfterDays asleep (7 days away in all since 0.1.14; was 3) they leave the world and their things stay where they slept. A grave marks where someone died for graveHours. idleMinutes: if you're in the game but don't touch anything for this long, your person goes on autopilot and does the same, until you tap. sleepBelow: someone on autopilot or away lies down to sleep when Rest is under this, and gets up when it's full. At night (see night) they go to sleep until morning. comeBackSeconds: for this long after a player's connection goes, their person stays right where they are, so a short break in the connection changes nothing (the game carries on from where it was). With a claim (see claims) they stay within it instead of by the pond, keep its fire fed from their bag, and still walk to the pond to drink.
help.berryBushes: extra: how many more berry bushes grow out in the wider world, besides the ones by the start. seed: their own random numbers, so they're in the same places on every phone (change it to move them all).
help.tips: First-steps tips for someone new, shown one at a time in the pill above the needs, each once per phone. words: what each says, in the order they come (walk, pickup, rings, food, craft). Each goes once the player has done what it says, or after show seconds. The next waits gap seconds, or pace seconds if the last one wasn't tried. A tip for something already done is never shown. A new tip needs its rule in game/tips.js (TIP_RULES) too. Friendly full sentences, short enough for two lines on a phone. Luke picked these five (25 Nov 2026): ask him before adding another.
help.devlog: What's new, shown in the Menu. Newest first, one entry per version: version, date (the release day, with from for a range), an optional title, and short lines for players in added (+ new features), improved (~ changes to what's there) and fixed (− bug fixes and removed issues). No full stop at the end.
help.energyCosts: Stamina (the yellow ring, id energy) is short-term: every task takes these amounts and walking takes walkPerMetre for each metre. It comes back by itself quickly (perHour in its need: 600 an hour, so empty to full in about 10 minutes; whileAsleep 1500 when sleeping, whileSitting 2400 when sitting by a fire). Below slowBelow (20) your person is out of breath: walking and tasks take slowBy (1.5) times as long. It never stops you and it's not deadly. The server uses the same numbers. dig is digging or flattening a farm field, plant is planting seeds.
help.chopping: Chopping with a tool (tool: the item you need). tree: chopping a standing tree (seconds, and what falls: gives); it leaves a stump that grows back into a tree after regrowDays real days: a number, or [soonest, latest] so each stump takes its own time in between (stumpBackMs in rules.js). stump: digging out a stump (then the tree is gone for good). log: chopping a log (an item) into sticks. Each chop wears the tool by one use, and takes energyCosts.chop energy. The server uses the same rules.
help.plants: Plants you cut, like tall grass. Each kind is laid out by itself: count clumps (nearStart of them near the start), on its own random numbers (seed) so nothing else moves. action is the tap menu button, verb what shows while doing it. gives goes into your inventory each cut. seconds is how long by hand, toolSeconds with the tool (each use wears the tool). regrowHours [lo, hi]: a cut clump grows back at a random time in between. look: blades per clump, height, colour and tips (the seed heads). Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing plants.
help.regions: The worlds (regions) on the main menu, under Play. Each is its own world on its own clock (timeZone). open: false shows it as Coming soon; tapping it shows this world's view at that region's time of day. For now only one world exists, so only one region can be open, and its timeZone should match settings.worldTimeZone.
help.night: Night in the world's clock (settings.worldTimeZone), from the hour 'from' to the hour 'to'. Sleeping at night fills Rest at whileAsleepAtNight instead of whileAsleep. People away or on autopilot go to sleep when night starts and get up in the morning. The server uses the same numbers.
help.placeables: Things you place in the world and build, like the campfire. An item with places (the id of an entry here) gets a Place button in the Inventory: you pick a spot, your person puts it down as an unbuilt site, then builds it (buildSeconds; buildVerb shows while building). solid is how big it is for walking round (metres). size is the squares it takes on the placing grid ([across, deep]; each square is half a metre, 2 x 2 if left out), and it can be turned 4 ways. keepClear: other placed things stay at least this many metres from its square (the campfire keeps room for its seats); without it things can go side by side. The ground under a placed thing is levelled (game/land.js); settings.placeMaxRise is the most the ground may rise and fall (metres) under a spot for something to go there. fire makes it a fire you can light and put out: fuel is the item you add (sticks), secondsEach is how long one burns (900 = 15 minutes), otherFuels are more items it burns with their seconds each (log: 43200, 12 hours; twig: 300, 5 minutes), maxHours is the most it holds in hours of burning (168 = 7 days, so a claim's fire can last the 7-day away timer; without maxHours, maxFuel counts it in fuel items), lightSeconds how long lighting takes. It only burns while lit, keeps burning while players are away, and goes out by itself when the fuel runs out. seats: people can sit round it (count places, distance metres from the middle). Sitting is a task with no set time: your person sits until you stand up, do something else or the fire goes out, and keeps sitting while you're away. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing placeables. craftLabel names the tap menu list of recipes made there (recipes with near), like Cook. madeWith (0.1.18, the farm field) makes it something you dig with a tool instead of placing from an item: the tool (the stone hoe) has to be on your tool bar, it takes makeSeconds (makeVerb shows meanwhile) and a use of the tool, it's ready straight away (no building), and the same tool flattens it again (flattenSeconds). inCamp: it can only go in your own camp. look (only for one made with a tool) is how it's drawn: shape field is tilled soil (colour, ridge).
help.mining: Mining with a tool (tool: the item you need, the stone pickaxe). rock: breaking a small rock (seconds, and what falls: gives); the rock is then gone, but one broken rock comes back by a boulder every rockBackHours. boulder: mining a boulder; gives can be a range like [3, 5]. A mined boulder stays (it can't be removed) and can be mined again after regrowDays real days (the same as trees). Each hit wears the tool by one use and takes energyCosts.chop energy. The server uses the same rules.
help.liveSettings: Numbers the admin can change live from the Admin panel (Settings tab) without a new build. Each one's id is wired up in code (server/src/live.js and test/game/admin.js); name, group, unit, min, max and step are just how it shows. The normal value still comes from the rest of this file (settings, chopping, mining, sources, stats); a live change wins until the admin taps Reset.
help.testNames: Only for testing: with settings.autoName on, Make your person fills in a random name from this list. autoName is off in the real game, so players type their own name (the checks in tools/tests switch it on for themselves).
help.bodyShapes: How each body is drawn, one for each choice in looks.sex (female, male): its height and how wide or long each part is. The builds on Make your person (looks.build: slim, medium, broad) then make it wider or narrower. A new looks.sex choice needs an entry here with the same id.
help.claims: Claims (players see a claim as a camp: docs/design/wording.md): your first campfire becomes your claim when you light it: radius metres round it, yours only while the fire burns (once it's out the land is free and anyone can take the cold fire apart). One claim each. Claims can't overlap and can't reach into the free area round the main pond (spawnRadius metres from the pond's middle; the pond itself is about 6 m across from its middle). Inside someone else's claim others can only walk through. placeable: the kind that claims. ringShowsWithin: how near you have to be to see a claim's faint ring. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing it.
help.societies: Player groups inside the world (built 0.1.4, reworked 0.1.5). Players see a society and its claim as one camp (0.1.6: Menu > Camp, Invite to camp); only the code and the admin say society and claim. Your claim is your society: lighting your first campfire starts both (named "<name>'s camp" until the leader renames it, 2 to nameMax letters, no two the same) and the fire going out ends both. Up to maxMembers people (also a live setting, Admin > Settings). Members can do everything in the claim and keep its fire fed; only the leader can put it out; their own fires are just fires. The leader invites someone playing within inviteReach metres; they have inviteMinutes to tap Join, and must put out their own claim's fire (or leave their society) first. Anyone can leave; the leader can remove people. If the leader leaves or is gone, the member who joined first leads. The last one out ends it and its fire goes out. A player with no person in the world for 3 days (the away timer) leaves.
help.crops: Crops (0.1.18, farming): what grows on a farm field. seed is the item you plant (it's used up), on is the placeable it grows on (field), growHours how long it takes from planting to grown (it grows by itself, a sprout, then a small bush, then a full one), plantSeconds how long planting takes, and like is the source whose rules it follows once grown (berryBush: what picking gives, how many it holds, how fast they grow back, the knife picking 2). A field takes one crop; flattening the field loses it. The admin's Settings tab has one live number for how long every crop takes (Farming, Planted crops grow in).

words.walk: Double-tap the ground to walk. Tap anything to see what you can do.
words.pickup: Tap a stick or a stone on the ground, then Pick up.
words.rings: The rings are your needs. Tap them to see what each one is.
words.food: Pick berries from a bush and eat them from your inventory. Drink at the pond.
words.craft: Open your inventory and tap Recipes to make things. Try a sharp stone first.

devlog.title: Farming
added: Stone hoe: a hoe head (stone and twine), then a long stick and twine
Dig farm fields in your camp with the hoe, and flatten them again
Berry seeds: cut a berry on the craft mat with a sharp stone
Plant berry seeds on a field and a berry bush grows in about a day
Pick your planted bush like a wild one, and a knife picks 2 at once
fixed: Picking berries with a knife shows both berries straight away

added: A tool bar above your inventory with 7 spots, and tools on it weigh nothing
Equip a tool from your inventory, or drag it onto the tool bar (onto a tool to swap them)
improved: Campfires snap to a half-metre grid and turn 4 ways with the Turn button
The ground under placed things is levelled so nothing sits half in a hill
fixed: Tools are held in the right hand, and only that hand swings when you use them
Feet no longer sink into the ground when bending, kneeling or standing on a slope

improved: Quicker to cut grass by hand, mine a boulder and cook fish
Mined boulders come back in a day, and stumps grow back into trees in 1 to 2 days
Recipes now has its own tab at the top of your inventory, in place of the Craft button
The craft mat shows the recipe you tap, then Make. No more putting things on it by hand
Your person stays in the world for 7 days while you're away, up from 3
A campfire holds up to 7 days of fuel, up from 3
Fuel burns longer: logs 12 hours, sticks 15 minutes, twigs 5 minutes
More stones and tall grass around the world

added: Play on other devices, in Settings: link your phone and computer with a code
improved: Greyed out in Recipes now means you don't have everything for it yet
Names are one of a kind: you can't pick a name someone in the world already has
fixed: Tapping a recipe could show something else on the mat, like a sharp stone for a campfire

added: Leave the world for good, in Settings: your person and everything about you is removed
A loading screen while the world gets ready, so Play always works when you see it
An app icon, and a picture and a few words when you share the game's link
Privacy and rules in Settings: what the game keeps, and the rules for playing
Tips for your first steps: walking, picking up, your needs, food and water, crafting
improved: Making your person now fits a phone held sideways
The game says when it can't reach the world, and what to check
The first load is a little quicker
The main menu is easier on your battery
Things left on the ground for 7 days fade away. Things in a camp stay
Privacy and rules says more: why things are kept, your choices, help if you're under 18
Recipes under the craft mat lists everything you can make, greyed out until made
Tap any recipe to put what it takes on the mat, so there's no guessing
Bag under the craft mat is now called Inventory
fixed: Tapping something another player had just picked up could cause an error
The Send button in chat slipped off the edge of very small phones
At night the main menu showed daylight for a moment before going dark

added: New to crafting? The craft mat suggests trying two stones to start
improved: New recipes for the stone axe and pickaxe: a stone head, a long stick and twine
Cutting a stick with a sharp stone gives 2 twigs
A campfire weighs 9 now, the same as the things it takes
Food is only cooked at a lit campfire now, not on the craft mat

devlog.title: The craft mat
added: Craft mat: put things from your inventory together and discover what they make
Found list: tap a recipe you've made to put its things back on the mat
New things to make: sharp stone, twig, long stick, axe head and pick head
improved: Craft is in your inventory now, so the hammer button at the bottom is gone
Tools are made in steps now, like a sharp stone first, then a stone knife
A campfire takes a log, 2 twigs and 2 stones, and twigs burn as quick fuel
Recipes you find stay with you when you start again as a new person

added: Your person carries on with your task list while you're away, then looks after themselves
improved: Your person keeps working while the Menu, Camp or What's new is open
Welcome back says how many things on your task list got done
Your campfire's land and your group are now one thing, called your camp
Clearer wording all over, and tap menus now match the task list
fixed: Eating and drinking now show +10 food or +15 water, not +10 Hunger
Fish is now called raw fish, so it's clear it needs cooking
The Menu no longer says Paused, since the world keeps going

improved: Lighting your first campfire starts your camp, and it ends when that fire goes out
The leader can rename the camp in Menu > Camp
Only the leader can put the camp's fire out
A camp's name shows under name tags once it has 2 or more people

added: Camps: groups of players who share one campfire's land. The leader invites people nearby
A camp shares the land round its leader's lit campfire. Members can use everything there
Your camp shows under your name
improved: Away members stay in their camp and keep its fire going

fixed: Tapping the feedback box no longer zooms the page in on iPhones

added: Dragged items go in your task list, with a see-through copy where they'll land
improved: Smoother dragging and inventory management
fixed: Queued items can't be moved or tapped again until their task is done

added: Drag a loose item on the ground to move it, or onto a campfire to burn it
improved: Items dragged out of the Inventory drop where you let go
Tidier version numbers: every update before this is now an early build (0.0.x)

devlog.title: Early builds
added: First playable: berry bushes, tap menus, the task list and the pause menu
One shared online world, with speech bubbles, a chat filter, Mute and Report
Your person stays in the world and looks after themselves while you're away
Rest and Stamina, sleeping, and one Darwin clock for everyone
Crafting and stone tools: chop trees, break rocks and cut tall grass for twine
Campfires, recipes you find as you go, and a grid inventory
Camps: your lit campfire makes the land round it yours
Fishing with a spear at the pond, and cooking fish on a campfire
Drag items out of the Inventory, and on a computer loose items glow under the mouse
improved: New dark glass look with needs as rings, and nicer sticks, stones, berries and logs
